about.title: Galt Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Galt is a small city, and when a fatal collision happens on A Street, C Street, or one of the corridors feeding SR-99, its effects ripple through neighborhoods and families quickly. Even though public crash records for the most recent year show zero traffic deaths, serious injury collisions still occur here, and any one of them can turn tragic. Under California law, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal proceedings that may follow a fatal crash. It exists to help surviving family members address the practical and emotional toll of losing someone: funeral costs, lost income the person would have provided, and the loss of their guidance and companionship. Because standing to file is limited to certain spouses, domestic partners, children, or dependents, and because the filing window is generally two years from the date of death (shorter if a government entity is involved), it helps to understand your options early. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney, free of charge, to walk through what your family may be entitled to.

whyChoose.title: Why Galt Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain other dependents or heirs. An attorney can help clarify where your family stands before any deadline approaches.

items.title: A Claim Separate From Any Criminal Case
items.desc: A wrongful death lawsuit is a civil matter distinct from criminal charges the at-fault driver may face. Families can pursue this path regardless of how, or whether, a criminal case proceeds.

items.title: Recognizing What Losses Can Be Addressed
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An independent attorney can help you understand how these apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in Galt?
items.answer: Generally, California gives surviving family members two years from the date of death to file. That window can be shorter if a government entity, such as a public roadway agency, was involved in the crash. Speaking with an attorney soon after a loss helps preserve your options.

items.question: Does Galt's small size or low fatal-crash count affect our claim?
items.answer: No. Public records showing zero traffic deaths in the most recent year for Galt don't change the legal rights of a family who has lost someone in a crash on local roads like SR-99 or Twin Cities Road. Each case is evaluated on its own facts, not on citywide statistics.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim under California law?
Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim under California law?
items.answer: California generally gives priority standing to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can review your family's circumstances to determine who may file.
